chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Adamy narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Siyari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, on the authority of one who informed him, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, God, the Mighty and Exalted, has exempted our followers from six characteristics: insanity, leprosy, vitiligo, being born out of adultery (or having a child born out of adultery), and begging from the people with their hand.

key_terms.الْأَبَنَةِ: being born out of adultery / having a child born out of adultery
key_terms.شِيعَتَنَا: our followers (specifically referring to the Shia)

ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics from which God protects the Shia according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the spiritual and physical purity of the Shia community, linking their adherence to the Imams with divine protection from specific ailments and social stigmas. This enumeration serves as a theological assurance of their distinct status, emphasizing that their devotion shields them from both internal defects like insanity and external markers of impurity such as leprosy or illegitimacy. The inclusion of 'begging' underscores a culture of self-sufficiency and dignity within the community, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on maintaining honor through faith.
